Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City ht_tp://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 19 s. 2021 3 February 2021 ENGR. REMIE P. CONTE Manager/Owner Conte Builders & Construction Supply J. Prudente Street, Poblacion llaya San Enrique, Iloilo Dear Engr. Conte: This has reference to your letter dated 08 June 2020 requesting this Department's legal opinion relative to the imposition of tax by the Local Government Unit (LGU) of Dumangas, Iloilo with respect to a national government project being effected within its jurisdiction. In the aforesaid communication, it was averred that the additional tax imposed by the LGU of Dumangas will result to excessive discretionary authority on the part of the latter based on the following grounds: 1. All local and business taxes due to the Municipality of San Enrique, Iloilo, being the company's official business address, has already been paid; 2. Taxes due to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) were likewise paid and correspondingly settled; 3. The companys activities in the Municipality of Dumangas, which serves as the project site of the construction, are limited only to the scope of works. Lastly, it is asserted that the Municipality of Dumangas is the only LGU which imposes business tax to contractors undertaking national government projects.

It is therefore this Department's understanding that the issue herein is "Whether or Not the LGU of Dumangas, Iloilo can validly impose business tax on Conte Builders & Construction Supply, despite the fact that it is not where the principal office is located". Central to the controversy at hand is the application of Section 150 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), and Article 243 of Administrative Order No. 270-"Prescribing the Implementing Rules and Regulation of the LGC", in relation to Department of Finance (DOF)-Local Finance Circular No. 3-95, dated 22 May 1995, to wit: SECTION 150. Situs of the Tax. - (a) For purposes of collection of the taxes under Section 143 of this Code, manufacturers, assemblers, repackers, brewers, distillers, rectifiers and compounders of liquor, distilled spirits and wines, millers, producers, exporters, wholesalers, distributors, dealers, contractors, banks and other financial institutions, and other businesses, maintaining or operating branch or sales outlet elsewhere shall record the sale in the branch or sales outlet making the sale or transaction, and the tax thereon shall accrue and shall be paid to the municipality where such branch or sales outlet is located. In cases where there is no such branch or sales outlet in the city or municipality where the sale or transaction is made, the sale shall be duly recorded in the principal office and the taxes due shall accrue and shall be paid to such city or municipality. (b) The following sales allocation shall apply to manufacturers, assemblers, contractors producers, and exporters with factories, project offices, plants, and plantations in the pursuit of their business: (1) Thirty percent (30%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the principal office is located; and (2) Seventy percent (70%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the factory, project office, plant, or plantation is located. (c) In case of a plantation located at a place other than the place where the factory is located, said seventy percent (70%) mentioned in subparagraph (b) of subsection (2) above shall be divided as follows: (1) Sixty percent (60%) to the city or municipality where the factory is located; and

(2) Forty percent (40%) to the city or municipality where the plantation is located. (d) In cases where a manufacturer, assembler, producer, exporter or contractor has two (2) or more factories, project offices, plants, or plantations located in different localities, the seventy percent (70%) sales allocation mentioned in subparagraph (b) of subsection (2) above shall be prorated among the localities where the factories, project offices, plants, and plantations are located in proportion to their respective volumes of production during the period for which the tax is due. "Administrative Order No. 270, ARTICLE 243. Situs of the Tax. — (a) Definition of Terms — (I) Principal Office — the head or main office of the business appearing in the pertinent documents submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission, or the Department of Trade and Industry, or other appropriate agencies, as the case may be. The city or municipality specifically mentioned in the articles of incorporation of official registration papers as being the official address of said principal office shall be considered as the situs thereof. xxx (2) Branch or Sales Office — a fixed place in a locality which conducts operations of the business as an extension of the principal office. xxx (3) Project Office- shall mean the field office in the construction site. It is the equivalent to the factory of a manufacturer. Section 5, DOF Local Finance Circular No. 3-95: (b) For purposes of collection of the tax, the following rules shall apply: 4. 5. All gross receipts realized from domestic projects or contracts undertaken by the branch office shall be recorded in the said branch office and the tax thereon shall be payable to the city or municipality where the said branch is located; In cases where there is no branch office, the gross receipts from domestic projects or contracts shall be recorded in the Head/PrincipaI Office and the same shall be allocated as follows:

a. Thirty percent (30%) of the gross receipts shall be taxable by the city of municipality where the principal office is located; and b. Seventy percent (70%) of the gross receipt shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the project office is located. 6. In cases where there are two (2) or more project offices located in different localities, the seventy percent (70%) allocation stated in subparagraph (2)(ii) above shall be prorated among the localities where such project offices are located in proportion to the work accomplished based on the cost of the projects or contracts actually undertaken in the locality durinq the tax period for which the tax is due." (Emphasis and underscoring ours) The Supreme Court, in the case of City of Makati vs. Municipality of Bakun and Luzon Hydro Corporation, applied the foregoing and ruled that "the city/municipality specifically mentioned in the articles of incorporation as the official address of said principal office shall be considered as the situs of tax in the absence of branch or sales office. Otherwise, the branch or sales outlet shall record the sale in the branch or sales outlet making the sale or transaction, and the tax thereon shall accrue and shall be paid to the municipality where such branch or sales outlet is located. In cases where there is a factory, project office, plant or plantation in pursuit of business, thirty percent (30%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city/municipality where the principal office is located and seventy (70%) of all sales recorded in the principal office shall be taxable by the city or municipality where the factory, project office, plant or plantation is located. Based on the foregoing, it can be gleaned that the LGU of Dumangas, Iloilo, being the project site/office where the project is being implemented, can properly and lawfully impose business tax thereon pursuant to the abovementioned laws, guidelines and jurisprudence, in proportion to the work accomplished based on the cost of the projects or contracts actually undertaken therein during the tax period for which the tax is due. As admitted, the LGU of Dumangas serves as the project site wherein the scope of works are being conducted. As such, the LGU is entitled for an

allocation based on the business tax liability of Conte Builders & Construction Supply amounts to seventy percent (70%) of the gross receipt. Accordingly, LGU of Dumangas can validly impose business tax against Conte Builders in proportion to the scope of works accomplished therein. This opinion, however, shall be without prejudiced to the position of the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) of the Department of Finance (DOF) and other concerned agencies, as the subject matter herein falls within the ambit of their administrative competence and expertise. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Thank you Legal/91 Copy fumished: DIR. JUAN JOVIAN E. INGENIERO OIC, Regional Director DILG-Region VI 6 Pepita Aquino St Fort San Pedro Iloilo City Very truly yours, By uthority of the Secretary: OIC- RINGAN, CESO Ill ecretary for Local Govemment n
